title: The Ultimate Contrarian Trade?
gist: Teaser only: Gavekal questions whether the EU's new curbs on Chinese hybrid vehicle imports, and the broader deglobalization/reshoring consensus, are sustainable over the medium to long term. It argues the rising cost of funding government debt will become Western elected officials' first concern, implicitly setting up a reversal of protectionism as the contrarian trade; the full argument is paywalled.

themes.theme: Protectionism as fighting the last war

insights.claim: The EU has recently adopted measures limiting the sale of Chinese hybrid vehicles into Europe, which Gavekal frames as an example of policymakers fighting the last war.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: EU trade barriers on Chinese autos are the concrete test case for whether protectionist policy holds or gets unwound.
insights.quote: Take the recent measures adopted by the EU to limit the sale of Chinese hybrid vehicles into Europe as an example

insights.claim: Gavekal questions the consensus that deglobalization, great power rivalry, reshoring of manufacturing and the blocking of Chinese imports are durable trends, doubting that such protectionist policies will be sustainable over the medium to long term.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Positions built on a permanent deglobalization regime (reshoring beneficiaries, protected EU autos) carry reversal risk if the policy consensus cracks.
insights.quote: However, how sustainable will such policies prove to be over the medium to long term?

themes.theme: Debt funding costs as the binding constraint

insights.claim: Gavekal predicts that the rising cost of funding government debt will become the first concern of elected officials across most of the Western world in the coming months, quarters and years.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Sovereign funding costs, rather than strategic rivalry, may become the dominant driver of Western policy choices, putting bond yields at the center of the political agenda.
insights.quote: Let me suggest this: it will be the rising cost of funding of government debt.

insights.claim: The teaser implies that pressure from rising government debt funding costs will undermine the sustainability of protectionist policies such as the EU's curbs on Chinese hybrids, making a bet against protectionism the potential 'ultimate contrarian trade'; the mechanism is not spelled out in the visible text.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If fiscal stress forces Western governments to drop costly protectionism, assets that gain from renewed China-West trade could be mispriced against the deglobalization consensus.
